note: Faithful rendering of the anjana and protection-wheel ritual commentary and the Dīpaṃkara/Vajradhara point; the inline glosses are clumsy but do not change the sense.

errors.english: the signs of extinction and so on appear
errors.why: ཟད་པར་ here is kṛtsna, the meditative 'totalities' (kasiṇa) that appear as signs through meditation, not 'extinction'.

fix.find: the signs of extinction and so on appear
fix.replace: the signs of the totalities (kṛtsna) and so on appear

note: A sound rendering of the series of illusion examples; one meditation term misread.

errors.why: ནམ་མཁའི་ཁམས་ is ākāśadhātu, the element/expanse of space; the supplied equivalent 'dharmadhatu' is wrong.

note: Generally accurate Mahāmudrā commentary; one wrong Sanskrit equivalent, and 'shown' for སྟོན་གྱི (autumn's moon) is a minor slip.

errors.english: has perished, ceased, and does not exist. By saying "it undergoes change," it shows that there is no meeting of two moments of mind.
errors.why: The whole sūtra passage ('the mind by which one rejoices and dedicates ... has ended, ceased, gone, changed') is the quotation that shows the two minds do not meet; the English presents most of it as the commentator's reason and quotes only 'it undergoes change'.

errors.english: do not perish or cease; if they were to undergo change
errors.why: Parallel to the preceding sūtra line, the entities, objects, roots of virtue and merit are themselves 'ended, ceased, gone, changed'; the English says they do not perish or cease.

errors.english: Since that mind is the essence of non-existence, it is investigated

note: The Aṣṭasāhasrikā dedication passage is followed in outline, but quotation boundaries and the status of the 'ended, ceased' sequence are confused.
Accurate rendering of the Vyākhyāyukti close: the Sūtrālaṃkāra verses, the five qualities of the Buddha's speech, and the two speakers' purities.

errors.why: རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་ཚོགས་ is 'Collection/Mass of Jewels', not Ratnamālā ('Garland'); the note gives a wrong title as if it were the original.

note: Sound translation of the purity and observance verses with their glosses; only the title note is misleading.

errors.english: which no (shramana), (brahmin), god, (mara), Brahma, or anyone else in the world can rightfully turn back
errors.why: The Tibetan says no one else can turn (set in motion) this wheel in accordance with Dharma, not 'turn back' it.

note: Faithful to the three knowledges and the fearlessness formula, including the e-text's own dittography; one formulaic phrase shifted.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on own-characteristic and particular characteristic and the impermanence and truths glosses.

errors.english: the (Siddhartha) white mustard and (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated
errors.why: Continuing གསེར་ from the previous side, the pegs are 'made of gold and of khadira'; there is no white mustard here (it appears only later as an anointing substance).

fix.find: the (Siddhartha) white mustard and (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated
fix.replace: the [pegs] made of gold and of (Khadira) acacia catechu are consecrated

note: The deity lists, quarters and colours of the 28 wrathful pegs are rendered correctly; the opening misidentifies the peg material.

errors.english: Depart out of fear at his mere command,
errors.why: In the context of the vajra finger-snap gathering all Buddhas, གཤེགས་ means they came (were summoned), not that they departed.

fix.find: Depart out of fear at his mere command,
fix.replace: Come, frightened at his mere command,

note: Good rendering of the wrathful-manifestation verses and commentary; one verse inverts the summoning.
